Heard Sri Prem Chandra Dwivedi, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Babul Kumar Sharma,
learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 and Sri Anish Kumar Upadhyay, learned AGA for the State.

The present application has been filed to quash the entire proceeding including summoning order dated 02.05.2019 in Complaint Case No. 3185 of 2018, u/s 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P.
Act, P.S. Mahila Thana Navabad, District Jhansi, (Smt. Neelam Vs. Shankti Singh Pathraur and others), pending in the court of Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 1, Jhansi.

sentences.text: Contention of the counsel for the applicants is that matrimonial dispute between the applicant no. 1 and opposite party no. 2 has culminated into the impugned proceedings and on the basis of general allegations, entire family of the applicant no. 1 has been implicated.

It is further submitted that from the perusal of statement of opposite party no. 2 recorded u/s 200 Cr.P.C. it is clear that the Shakti Singh Pathraur And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115950884/
1 allegation is only against the applicant no. 1 but the court below erroneously summon the applicant nos. 2 and 3.
Per contra, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 has submitted though the opposite party no.
2 has not made any allegation in her statement u/s 200 Cr.p.C. but in her complaint the allegation of demand of dowry and harassment was also made against the applicant nos. 2 and 3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA has adopted the argument of learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 and submitted that prima facie case is made out against the applicants, therefore, no ground for interference is made out.

With the consent of the parties this case is finally disposed of without calling any counter affidavit from the opposite party no. 2 as the opposite party no. 2 has submitted that he does not propose to file any counter affidavit and want to argue the case on the basis of available record.

Considering the rival submissions of the counsel for the parties and on perusal of record, it appears that though in the impugned complaint general allegation was made against all the applicants but in the statement of opposite party no. 2 recorded u/s 200 Cr.P.C. no allegation was made against the applicant nos. 2 and 3, therefore, summoning the applicant nos. 2 and 3 is totally erroneous.
However, from the perusal of the complaint as well as statement of opposite party no. 2, it is clear that there are specific allegations against the applicant no. 1, therefore, no ground for interference is made out so far as applicant no. 1 is concerned, therefore, the present application is rejected on behalf of applicant no. 1.

However, from the perusal of the complaint as well as statement of opposite party no. 2 recorded u/s 200 Cr.P.C., it is clear that there is no allegation against the applicant nos. 2 and 3 therefore, no case is made out against the applicant nos. 2 and 3.
Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Achin Gupta Vs. State of Haryana & Anr. in Criminal appeal No.
2379 of 2024 as well as in the case of Geeta Malhotra and Another Vs. State of U.P. And Another (2012) 10 SCC 741 has observed that there is tendency to falsely implicates to family members and close relative of husband in matrimonial case on the basis of general allegations.
Paragraph nos. 32 and 35 of the Achin Gupta's Case (Supra) is being quoted as under:-
"32.

sentences.text: Many times, the parents including the close relatives of the wife make a mountain out of a mole.

Instead of salvaging the situation and making all possible endeavours to save the marriage, their action either due to ignorance or on account of sheer hatred towards the husband and his family members, brings about complete destruction of marriage on trivial issues.
The first thing that comes in the mind of the wife, her parents and her relatives is the Police, as if the Police is the panacea of all evil.
No sooner the matter reaches up to the Police, then even if there are fair chances of reconciliation between the spouses, they would get destroyed.
The foundation of a sound marriage is tolerance, adjustment and respecting one another.

sentences.text: each other's fault to a certain bearable extent has to be inherent in every marriage.
Petty quibbles, trifling differences are mundane matters and should not be exaggerated and blown out of proportion to destroy what is said to have been made in the heaven.

The Court must appreciate that all quarrels must be weighed from that point of view in determining what constitutes cruelty in each particular case, always keeping in view the physical and mental conditions of the parties, their character and social status.
A very technical and hyper sensitive approach would prove to be disastrous for the very institution of the marriage.
In matrimonial disputes the main sufferers are the children.
The spouses fight with such venom in their heart that they do not think even for a second that if the marriage would come to an end, then what will be the effect on their children.
Divorce plays a very dubious role so far as the upbringing of the children is concerned.
The only reason why we are saying so is that instead of handling the whole issue delicately, the initiation of criminal proceedings would bring about nothing but hatred for each other.
There may be cases of genuine ill-treatment and harassment by the husband and his family members towards the wife.
The degree of such ill-treatment or harassment may vary.
However, the Police machinery should be resorted to as a measure of last resort and that too in a very genuine case of cruelty and harassment.
The Police machinery cannot be utilised for the purpose of holding the husband at ransom so that he could be squeezed by the wife at the instigation of her parents or relatives or friends.
In all cases, where wife complains of harassment or ill-treatment, Section 498A of the IPC cannot be applied mechanically.
No FIR is complete without Sections 506(2) and 323 of the IPC.
Every matrimonial conduct, which may cause annoyance to the other, may not amount to cruelty.
Mere trivial irritations, quarrels between spouses, which happen in day-to-day married life, may also not amount to cruelty.

35. In one of the recent pronouncements of this Court in Mahmood Ali v. State of U.P., 2023 SCC OnLine SC 950, authored by one of us (J.B. Pardiwala, J.), the legal principle applicable apropos Section 482 of the CrPC was examined.

entities.text: Mahmood Ali v. State of U.P., 2023 SCC OnLine SC 950
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therein, it was observed that when an accused comes before the High Court, invoking either the inherent power under Section 482 CrPC or the extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution, to get the FIR or the criminal proceedings quashed,
essentially on the ground that such proceedings are manifestly frivolous or vexatious or instituted with the ulterior motive of wreaking vengeance, then in such circumstances, the High Court owes a duty to look into the FIR with care and a little more closely.

It was further observed that it will not be enough for the Court to look into the averments made in the FIR/complaint alone for the purpose of ascertaining whether the necessary ingredients to constitute the alleged offence are disclosed or not as, in frivolous or vexatious proceedings, the court owes a duty to look into many other attending circumstances emerging from the record of the case over and above the averments and, if need be, with due care and circumspection, to try and read between the lines."

sentences.text: In view of the above, proceeding of complaint case no. 3185 of 2018 is quashed so far as the applicant nos. 2 and 3 are concerned.
However, court below is free to proceed against applicant no.1, on whose behalf, present application has been rejected.

However, it is further provided that if the applicant no.1 appears before the court below and applies for bail, within a period of 15 days, then his bail application shall be considered in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another, reported in (2021) 10 SCC 773.

entities.text: Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another, reported in (2021) 10 SCC 773
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With the aforesaid observation, the present application stands disposed of.
